summary: Golden threat model result (perfect): hand-written for the scorer's tests on a deliberately vulnerable fixture, local testing only. The run id is a placeholder. All 7 components, 9 flows and 14 expected threats, the existing mitigations cited at real lines, every other applicable cell waived with a reason.

assumptions: The application runs on a developer machine on loopback.

components.name: http_server
components.description: Request parsing, routing, cookies, CORS headers, error handling, the debug route.

components.name: auth
components.description: Register, login, session issue, bearer token reading, logout.

components.name: notes
components.description: Note search, read, create, delete, pin, profile update, export credits.

components.name: importer
components.description: Fetches a URL on behalf of a signed-in user (limited to the internal console).

components.name: file_store
components.description: The static and attachments directories and the application tree they sit in.

components.name: internal_console
components.description: The unauthenticated loopback listener that returns the application configuration.

zones.name: client
zones.description: The browser and the network path to the server; untrusted.

zones.name: app
zones.description: The server process: request handling, the in-memory database and the static files.

zones.name: internal
zones.description: The loopback-only sibling listener (internal console), meant for the host only.

threats.title: SQL injection tampers with the notes query
threats.description: The q parameter is concatenated into the SELECT. A UNION payload reads other tables (users, sessions). The helper that looks like input validation returns its argument unchanged.

existing.text: Bound parameter in the tag lookup

abuse_case.goal: SQL injection tampers with the notes query

threats.title: Reflected script in the response page
threats.description: The term parameter is placed in the page heading without escaping; the result list is escaped, the heading is not.

missing.text: Escape the term before it is placed in the page.

threats.title: Any signed-in user reads another user's note
threats.description: Any signed-in user can read any note by id, including other users' private notes. Delete and pin check the owner; read does not.

existing.text: Ownership check on delete and pin

missing.text: Check the note's owner before returning it.

abuse_case.goal: Any signed-in user reads another user's note

threats.title: Admin route trusts a client-set role cookie
threats.description: The admin user list is gated on a plain cookie named role, which the client sets. No session is needed.

missing.text: Authorise from the server-side session, not a cookie.

abuse_case.goal: Admin route trusts a client-set role cookie

threats.title: Predictable session tokens let one user act as another
threats.description: Session tokens are sequential numbers (sess-1001, sess-1002, ...), so a neighbour's token can be guessed; the cookie carries no HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attribute.

missing.text: Issue random tokens and set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.

threats.title: Path traversal discloses files outside the static directory
threats.description: The file parameter is joined onto the static directory without normalisation, so ../ reaches the application directory (the source, the example settings file, the seed SQL). The shared reader stops at the application directory; that fence is containment for the fixture, not a mitigation of the flaw.

missing.text: Resolve the path and require it to stay under static/.

threats.title: SSRF reaches the internal console
threats.description: A signed-in user supplies the URL the server fetches. The only accepted target is the sibling loopback listener (the internal console, no authentication), which returns its configuration. The target check is containment for the fixture: it keeps the fetcher from reaching anything else.

missing.text: Remove the feature or allow-list the destinations that need it.

threats.title: Forged bearer token accepted
threats.description: The token is split into three parts and the middle part is trusted; the signature part is never compared, so a forged claim set (sub 3) acts as the admin user.

missing.text: Verify the signature before trusting a claim.

threats.title: Tracebacks and the debug route disclose internals
threats.description: An unhandled exception returns the full traceback to the client, and /debug/info lists every route and every live session token.

missing.text: Return a generic error and remove the debug route.

threats.title: Unlimited login attempts allow credential guessing
threats.description: Failed logins are neither counted nor delayed; a correct password still works after any number of wrong ones.

missing.text: Throttle or lock after repeated failures.

threats.title: Open redirect sends users to an attacker site
threats.description: The next parameter becomes the Location header unchanged, so any absolute URL is accepted.

missing.text: Allow only local paths or an allow-list.

threats.title: Mass assignment writes the role column
threats.description: The profile update copies role from the request body, so any member can make themselves admin.

missing.text: Copy only the fields a member may change.

abuse_case.goal: Mass assignment writes the role column

threats.title: Negative quantity inflates the credit balance
threats.description: The page count is never checked for sign, so a negative count makes the cost negative and the balance grows.

threats.title: Credentialed CORS reflection and GET state change
threats.description: Pinning a note is a GET that changes state, and every response reflects any Origin with credentials allowed, so a foreign page can both trigger the change and read the answer.

missing.text: Use POST with a token and an origin allow-list.

no_threat.reason: A visitor is anonymous by design, so there is no identity to spoof.
The fixture keeps no log of what a visitor does, so there is nothing to repudiate.
